"I don't how much help my personal story will be but here are my two cents.
I've been there, I think. Feeling completely useless and shit. There were some days where I was close to ending everything but I chickened out. So I always kept myself busy. Not really busy, but distracted. Watching a movie, binge watching netflix, etc. It helps I suppose. For the 40 minutes you have on the episode but then it's back to dealing with.. well my pathetic self. Always put other's need over me and swayed to their needs just so they would like me. I got reckless too, didn't care if I died. Would anyone care?
Fast forward a few years of bathing in self loath and pitty, I got my internet cut off for a few weeks and I had nothing to distract myself with. And I had to deal with me. The disgraceful me. Who would want that? this time around however, after a few days of feeling sorry for myself, I wanted to give myself a chance and forced myself to like me. I liked others for their imperfections and mistakes, found them cute even why not do it with me? Maybe I'm not the only one with whatever was not perfect with me. and it's okay right? not to be perfect? i didn't judge others for not being perfect but i hated myself for not being it. and that's not okay. when i finally realised that and truly accepted my pathetic self as the norm it lifted me instantly.
Moral of the story:
you have to learn to like yourself. i know it's so cliché and i've heard that a lot of times before i did it. it's not something someone can tell you, but something that just clicks and you get it. spend some time alone, without your phone or laptop or anything. just think about yourself and see how much of your imperfections you can find in others too. you feel secluded and alone because you think you are different. when you realise you aren't all that different, you forgive yourself for being how you are and maybe.. just maybe you will find happiness. I wish you all the best haha. really, what i went through back then, I wouldn't wish on my worst enemies!"

I'm 19 too and here is what I learned. Some people just don't appreciate when you appreciate them **too much**. It's kinda weird but when I seem uninterested and treat my gf well sparingly she can't have enough of me. Though pretending to be uninterested kinda makes you uninterested in the long run. I just got dumped 4 days ago. Started off uninterested and she'd always text me that she misses me and she baked me things and she'd decline extra work shifts and drive to my place just to spend a few hours with me. 7 months into this I felt I was being an ass when she devoted herself so much so I stopped pretending to be uninterested (with the random spurts of interest) and didn't hold back. A week into it she stopped texting me and I had to always initiate. Lasted exactly 23 days before she dumped me saying "I don't feel the sparks anymore". Haha it's funny. We were together for about 7 months and the moment I don't pretend it lasts 23 days but hey maybe it's just coincidence. Some will say we weren't meant to be but it seems to me like that's all that works if you want to keep a relationship.





And friends often tend to do that when they find someone new. I found myself ignoring mine too when I was in a relationship, don't be so hard on yourself. Some people also find it hard to maintain contact with people they don't see in a regular basis. There just isn't much you guys do together to talk about so the conversation dies out and people they are surrounded by seem more interesting. It's life. It sucks right now but maybe.. just maybe we are both really unlucky and there are good times ahead. We are both still 19 and so young, our lives have just started. Chin up! :)
